Mustali groups emerged during periods of great turmoil or during times when important teachings of the faith were in danger of being lost. They inspired movements and often took leadership roles, contributing to numerous reforms throughout history.

historical_references.reference: Mustali was a title given to Shia Imams who claimed descent from the Prophet Muhammad through Fatimah al-Zahra and her husband Ali. This title emerged during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 CE) when the Shia community in Iraq sought to distinguish themselves from the Sunni majority. Mustali Imams were believed to possess special spiritual and political authority and were revered as the rightful leaders of the Shia community.
historical_references.context: Shia community in Iraq distinguishing themselves from Sunni majority

historical_references.reference: The name Mustali is also associated with certain Shia sects, such as the Nizari Ismailis, who emerged in the 11th century CE. They were also believed to possess the power to grant spiritual and temporal authority to their followers.
